reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G2-MG-Q4-Live-v2 (mat_g2_mg_q4_2), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples strictly evaluate the core requirement of the competency: to solve problems involving elapsed time. Examples include elapsed minutes ("A class started at 9:15 a.m. and ended at 9:35 a.m. How many minutes did it last?"), elapsed hours ("The community sports festival started at 10:00 a.m. and lasted for 6 hours."), elapsed days ("A school sports meet begins on Thursday and finishes on Saturday"), and interpreting timetables ("Look at the bus timetable:").

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All dimensions specified in the competency are present in the sample. It includes questions calculating minutes in an hour (e.g., "How many minutes long is the English class?"), hours in a day (e.g., "after running for 6 hours. What time did it start?"), days in a week (e.g., "How many days does the art workshop run?"), and specifically integrates timetables as directed (e.g., "According to the timetable, how many minutes is the travel time for Bus 2?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive load and complexity are perfectly tailored for Grade 2. The minute intervals are bounded to simple subtraction within an hour or crossing an hour cleanly using familiar 5-minute increments (e.g., "started at 12:45 p.m. and ended at 1:35 p.m."). Hours are small whole numbers ("lasted for 6 hours"), and days are within a single week (e.g., "begins on Tuesday and finishes on Friday"), which avoids cognitive overload while testing the core concepts.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The packet provides a comprehensive array of problem types. It requires finding the elapsed duration given start and end times ("How many minutes did it last?"), finding the end time given a start time and duration ("What time did it end?"), and finding a start time given the end time and duration ("The train journey ended at 5:00 p.m. after running for 6 hours. What time did it start?"). This ensures students understand the relationship between start time, end time, and elapsed time from all angles.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample question strictly targets elapsed time or timetables. There is no introduction of out-of-scope concepts like converting between minutes and seconds, calculating over multiple weeks, or dealing with complex 24-hour time formats. Every item firmly belongs to Grade 2 elapsed time.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The contexts used are relatable and realistic for young children, such as a "movie", "soccer practice", "art workshop", and "class schedule". The durations are logical for the scenarios (a 45-minute class, a 3-day sports meet, a 6-hour train journey), providing a mathematically sound and practical scale.
